Neurotoxic effects have been reported for many antineoplastics, including altretamine (p.678), asparaginase (p.682), busulfan (p.690), carboplatin (see under Incidence of Adverse Effects, p.693), carmustine (p.694), chlorambucil (p.696), chlormethine (p.697), cisplatin (p.698), cladribine (p.701), cytarabine (p.705), etanidazole (p.718), etoposide (p.718), fludarabine (p.721), fluorouracil (p.723), gemcitabine (p.728), hydroxycarbamide (p.729), ifosfamide (p.732), lomustine (p.741), methotrexate (p.746), mitotane (p.753), mitoxantrone (p.754), oxaliplatin (p.758), paclitaxel (p.759), pentostatin (p.763), procarbazine (p.765), tegafur (p.776), vinblastine (p.786), vincristine (p.787), and vindesine (p.788). In some cases these effects may be associated with par- ticular routes such as the intrathecal. See under the individual monographs for further details. Radiotherapy can also cause damage to the nervous system so combination of the two modal- ities may lead to additive effects. Reviews. 1. Verstappen CCP, et al.
